_meta.purpose: Doc 14 (Subject Global Parameters) encoded as SCOPE-BOUND, data-driven defaults. Each family names the exact module cohort/series/level it governs; a convention applies ONLY within that scope (authority model §3.1). Deferred assets/URLs/setup are emitted as VISIBLE 'Designer/Developer To Do:' red-note placeholders (never a hidden comment). Components owned by docs 03/04/05 are NOT re-owned — only the subject-specific CHOICE is recorded, with a cross_reference. Every class/snippet was supplied by the design team (doc 14); none are invented.
_meta.source: Doc 14 of the HTML Convertor knowledge base: 14_SUBJECT_GLOBAL_PARAMETERS.md
_meta.source_version: The 11-section version: 14.9 BLLR, 14.10 MiW/WJ, 14.11 cross-cutting; expanded Languages/Pathways/Taonga/LS/HPE.
_meta.authority: TOP within a family's stated scope only; OUTSIDE that scope the Granular_Scaffold_Registry (judged at the finest reliable grouping) is authoritative. A doc-14 default is cross-checked against the registry's series house-style after applying; disagreement raises a Red Flag (never a silent override).

gold_override_policy.rule: Doc-14 conventions are FORWARD-LOOKING design-team directives. The human gold library (01-Finalized_Modules_) largely PREDATES them, so the gold may not comply. For every family marked overrides_gold:true, ALL conversions adhere to the doc-14 convention EVEN WHERE the module's own human gold does not — within that family's scope, these rules sit ABOVE the LEVEL-0 own-gold target (its one recorded exception).
gold_override_policy.divergence_rule: Any comparison with the human gold that finds the converter diverging from it MUST first check whether the divergence matches a marked doc-14 convention in scope. A match is an INTENTIONAL, EXPECTED divergence — verdict 'DOC-14 OVERRIDE': do NOT 'fix' the converter back toward the gold on these points, and never count the divergence as a converter error.
gold_override_policy.sibling_structure_note: Doc-14's OWN internal hierarchy is preserved: for pure page STRUCTURE where a BUILT same-series sibling disagrees with a doc-14 convention, the sibling remains the most reliable structural reference (Mode B) and the conflict is surfaced as a visible Red Flag — the conflict is never silently resolved in either direction. For the CONVENTIONS doc-14 states (labels, copy, fonts, red-note placeholders, carve-outs, supplied snippets, per-subject choices), doc-14 wins over the gold outright.
gold_override_policy.gate_policy: How a live doc-14 emission is kept apart from comparisons with the (pre-doc-14) gold: (a) every red-note placeholder is emitted with class cv2-note IN ADDITION to the supplied inline style, so it is recognised as a converter note (visible form unchanged); (b) a STRUCTURAL doc-14 emission that diverges from the gold is a documented, intentional delta (rule id + affected pages), doc-14-mandated rather than editorial; (c) every family stays behind its `active` flag + SUBJECTPARAMS_OFF so the pre-doc-14 output can always be produced for comparison.

_meta.note: master_enabled:false keeps the output unchanged (the mechanism is wired + demonstrable but inert by default). Turn a family live one at a time via its `active` flag (see roadmap).
_meta.red_note_format: Designer/Developer To Do: {text}
_meta.live_emission_note:
When wired live, red-notes are emitted with class="cv2-note" ADDED to the supplied inline style (

…) so they are recognised as converter notes. The design-team-visible form is unchanged.
_meta.roadmap_note: Active families (BLL, LS, HPE content, CED P5) have concrete code-derivable triggers and are ready to wire live first. The asset-deferred families (Languages, Pathways, Taonga, BLLR, MiW) and FUNdamentals are mostly placeholder red-notes; their prefixes have little or no presence in 01-Finalized_Modules_, so their rules are forward-provisioning until those WTs arrive.

conventions.detail: Any interactive/text the ākonga reads or interacts with uses the writing font writeFont (writeFont.html, Playwrite NZ Basic). Ensure specifically: single-storey a, capital I reads as a capital I, single-storey g (these ākonga are just learning to read and write — the letters they read must match the letters they write; l and I are confusing when identical).

scope.label: LS modules (XLP toolkits + XDLS exemplars + LS content)

conventions.name: .learningSupport on <html>
conventions.detail: Root tag carries class 'notranslate learningSupport' (existing CSS hook; LS always carry it). Larger font (same as LS Whakatau).

conventions.name: Terminology + first-mention brackets
conventions.detail: hoa ako (learning partner); hua ako -> check -> hoa ako; learner -> ākonga; WE/US -> you. Brackets only on the FIRST instance a term is used in a module (first mention 'hoa ako (learning partner)', plain 'hoa ako' thereafter). CONTENT rule — flag, never auto-invent.

conventions.name: Remove tab navs (lesson-based, not inquiry)
conventions.detail: LS modules are lesson-based; remove tab navs (they carry too much media). Move-on prompts go at the bottom of each page.

conventions.name: clickDrop activity layout (choicePage, per-choice icons)
conventions.detail: Activity content rows sit in col-12 col-md-8; activity wrappers off col-md-10. iconType values: learnByHeart, explain, do, compare, judge, create.

conventions.name: Action prompts = colour-coded speech-bubble character
conventions.detail: In-page action prompts are man-with-speech-bubble, colour-coded to the module, bold heading (clear about what they are looking at) + bullet-point prompting questions — NOT activity boxes. General prompting questions also go in speech bubbles.

conventions.name: Many videos/images -> slideshow with caption text
conventions.detail: When a page has many videos/images, put them in a video/image slideshow with the body text as captions, plus prompting text (e.g. 'explore the slideshow to see examples of…').

conventions.name: 6-activity pattern: one dropbox at page bottom
conventions.detail: No activity numbers on clickDrop images (the pop-out number is not on the image). Remove all dropboxes from the activity boxes — ONE dropbox at the bottom of the page. Intro copy supplied ('Below are activities. You can choose the activities you feel will enhance your learning…'). Explicit titles: Learn about… / Explain why… / Practise… / Compare … versus … / Do you think…? / Create … Each activity: text explaining what to do; media (video or image); an invitation to share with kaiako. Compare activities add a Venn-diagram prompt ('You may like to use a Venn diagram to compare') + a 'What is a Venn diagram?' button (video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lnalI7eVQsQ&t=16s) + 'Here is an example of what your Venn diagram might look like.'

conventions.name: Dropbox copy + 'Upload to Dropbox' button
conventions.detail: Dropbox title 'Share your learning!'; body: 'When you have completed your chosen activities, upload your photos, videos or voice recordings to show your kaiako. If you require a specific media uploaded to the dropbox use the corresponding icon. When there is more than one type of media students can upload, use the generic dropbox button.'

conventions.name: End-of-page 'invitation to move forward' alerts (supplied copy)
conventions.detail: Exploratory: 'Ka pai! You've completed this lesson about _____ where we started to explore __learning intention__. Choose which lesson you would like to explore next! Click on the back button below to return to the introduction page and choose your next activity.' Lesson-by-lesson: 'Ka pai! You've completed lesson _, where we started to explore __learning intention__. Now let's try lesson _.' End of module: 'Ka pai! You have completed this module. We hope you enjoyed your learning. Discuss with your kaiako what topic you might like to explore next!'

conventions.name: XLP unique supervisor overview
conventions.detail: XLP = Learning Partner Toolkits (for supervisors) — unique overview, not the full ākonga-facing overview.

conventions.name: Standard LS overview (non-XLP)
conventions.detail: Overview tab: UKD, LI and SC. Information tab: Planning your time + What do I need to get started. Standards tab: Assessment for learning + the standards. Whakataukī in Te Reo AND English. First line: 'This module is called …' with an audio hover trigger over the Te Reo word. Second body text: purpose of the module. Media: video or photo. Then the move-forward prompt (text prompt if ordered lesson-by-lesson; if exploratory: 'Below are options you can select from. You can choose to start anywhere.' + buttons to pages, with the smaller words ('Move', 'Eat', etc.) removed).

rules.status: CAPTURED (the prohibition is satisfied live; the affirmative widths are not yet wired)
rules.name: Activity/interactive wrappers never col-md-10; generation-default widths by template family
rules.rule: An activity/interactive wrapper NEVER uses col-md-10. Generation defaults where no built same-series sibling dictates otherwise: Standard family -> col-12; Inquiry/Fundamentals (container-fluid body class) -> col-md-11 col-12; an activity paired with an alertImage -> activity col-md-8 col-12 + image col-md-4 (8+4=12, overrides the sub-type default). rules.v2_home: activity_wrapper templates (Emit_Templates) + the cascade; the affirmative widths are not yet wired (a documented DOC-14 delta per _meta.gold_override_policy.gate_policy when they are)
rules.measured_note: The converter never emits a col-md-10 activity wrapper (the box's inner col is col-12). In the gold, col-md-8 col-12 is by far the most common wrapper width; col-md-12, col-12, col-md-10 (pre-rule) and col-md-11 are minorities. Doc-14's own Mode-B rule (a built same-series sibling wins on pure STRUCTURE) governs the existing families, whose gold uses col-md-8 — so the affirmative widths apply to no-sibling-precedent generation (new families/modules); flipping the existing corpus wholesale would be wrong on the design team's own precedence. Never copy gold's col-md-10 minority.
rules.wj_carve_out_cl0065: CL-0065 (designer-confirmed): WJ-series (MiW, codes beginning WJ) wrapper widths are fit-based col-md-8 col-12 -> col-md-12 col-12; col-md-11 is NEVER used in WJ (widen straight to col-md-12 only when the interactive genuinely needs full width). rules.name: One interactive component per activity wrapper
rules.rule: Each activity wrapper contains at most ONE interactive component; a writer stacking 2+ under one activity heading splits into sequential LETTERED activities (the first keeps the writer's number, each next interactive takes the next letter) with FOLLOWING activities renumbered, every split flagged with a visible 'Red Flag:' note. Supporting elements (audio buttons/triggers, images, hover translations, instructional text) are NOT counted. The gold library largely PREDATES the rule — the gold often has 2+ interactive component groups in ONE box — and in the dominant multi-widget family (BLL phonics -02) the converter's box matches the gold box-for-box (e.g. 2C carousel+accordion), which a split would break; the other cases have no derivable discriminator, and the TRR/PNR boxes belong to the bilingual section-table boundary class, not this rule. So the rule is not wired live universally; it stands for FUTURE conversions: a divergence matching it (gold one-per-box lettered split vs converter multi, or vice versa where a future family adopts the rule) is an INTENTIONAL DOC-14-style override. When wired (per family): data home activity_wrapper.one_interactive_split, env ACTSPLIT_OFF, split at the widget-flow-into-open-activity emit seam riding the existing {lessonNumber}{letter} counter (ActivitiesBuilder.activityOpen) so follower renumbering falls out of the counter advance.
rules.v2_home: NOT LIVE — no engine path, no data flag yet (this entry IS the record).

The gold library largely PREDATES the universal form — gold's dominant widget-carrying anatomy is same_col (prose+widget in ONE inner col), so the universal flip is NOT live against the built corpus (doc-14 Mode-B: built gold/sibling structure wins; the same constraint family as the CL-0007 wrapper widths). The rule's SUBSTANCE is real gold behaviour where wrappers are widened: two-row boxes tie the prose col to the box's OUTER width (widened col-11/col-md-11 outer -> prose col-md-8 col-12, as in ENFUN; DEFAULT col-md-8 outer -> prose col-12) — i.e. CL-0036's widened form IS the gold convention, and it generalises per-family, not yet universally. In families that adopt the universal CL-0048 form, a divergence matching it is an INTENTIONAL override.

rules.status: CAPTURED (forward-looking; not wired live — the VIDEO-kind discriminator is not derivable from V2's inputs)
rules.name: CS-produced (Te Kura in-house / Audiovisual) VIDEO embeds the pending-ID Vimeo videoSection scaffold + a Designer/Developer To Do note
rules.rule: A CS-produced (Te Kura in-house / Audiovisual) VIDEO embeds the designer-supplied Vimeo videoSection scaffold with the ID pending (src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/"), preceded by a red+bold 'Designer/Developer To Do: add vimeo embed for [audiovisual item x]' note, keeping the trailing <!-- &start=0 --> <!-- &end=0 --> placeholders (a permitted comment exception alongside the Mode-P image reference + the ACK-TODO supplement). The [Audiovisual item N] / [AV item N] / [Audio visual item: N] / [Audiovisual request item N] marker family (BLL254-257, BLL270-276, ENGJ403, SSOG105; red-span forms resolve as data-marker SUBTAGs via the [Item N] alias, black/table-cell forms carry no tag at all) denotes CS media of ANY kind, mostly AUDIO (pronunciation sounds, mp3 voice-overs, an interactive hot-seating avatar), and no WT or Media List channel marks an item's kind. The golds of these modules use no vimeo; the gold's own pairing is per-KIND — audio → audioButton/audio-player scaffolds woven inside widget builds; animation → an EMPTY videoSection icon + red 'Designer note: Animation to come' (the pre-ledger form of this very rule); ENGJ403's gold has To Do notes for its AUDIO/avatar items. Emitting the vimeo VIDEO scaffold at the markers would be the wrong kind at most sites, so it is not wired; the rule STANDS for future conversions: when a WT/Media-List convention makes the video kind derivable (a new-era WT explicitly marking a CS video), it can be wired. A divergence matching the rule (gold vimeo vs converter youtube/nothing; or, once live, the pending-ID scaffold vs a gold real ID — the real ID IS the publish-time wiring) is an INTENTIONAL override.
rules.v2_home: NOT LIVE — no engine path, no data flag yet (this entry IS the record). Reserved home: data elements.cs_video_vimeo (scaffold template + note template + marker pattern), env VIMEOSCAFFOLD_OFF; the note is kind 'todo' via NotesAndComments.redFlag (red_flag.todo_form); the trailing &start/&end comments need a THIRD Emit_Templates._meta.comment_policy exception.

rules.status: LIVE (env EMOJISTRIP_OFF; Input_Doc_Rules.emoji_strip; ListsAndRuns.EmojiStrip full-page post-pass wired in PageAssembler)
rules.name: Emoji are stripped from rendered writer content (ticks & crosses exempt); 2+ emoji-prefixed lines become a <ul>; ONE red disclosure note per affected page
rules.rule:
The FIRST CL-0001/constraint-1 exception permitting deletion of writer characters: Unicode Extended_Pictographic grapheme CLUSTERS (base + VS15/16, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, keycap marks, flag pairs) are removed from the rendered page, EXCEPT the ledger's exempt ticks & crosses ✅✓✔☑✗✘❌❎ (kept cluster-whole — a VS16 is never orphan-stripped off a kept tick) and the ONE extension, the maths operators ✖➗➕➖ (meaning-bearing; the gold keeps ✖; ✖ is a cross by form — the ledger's own ☑ inclusion shows box/heavy variants count). EP arrow emoji (➡⬅⬆⬇⮕) become PLAIN arrows (→←↑↓) instead of deletions — the gold's own treatment (TEDC402 renders the writer's 'input🡪process🡪output' as 'input→process→output'); a keycap digit keeps its digit. A run of 2+ consecutive plain

lines PREFIXED by a would-be-deleted cluster becomes ONE

    /
  • (lead dropped); a lone one stays a

    ; in-prose removals get spacing normalised; a

    the strip EMPTIED is dropped whole. Disclosure: ONE visible note per affected page at the first removal — 'Red Flag: Emoji have been removed from this content per the no-emoji rule. Ticks and crosses are retained.' (the note scheme's form, class cv2-note; a header/menu first-removal relocates to the body top). OUT OF SCOPE by the Unicode property: the checkbox/ballot family ☐☒□🗹 (bilingual checklists + printable tick-sheets; the checklist→bullet stays the reo-menu machinery), 🖵 phonics sound-boxes, 🡪, plain →←, typographic ►●◦, private-use chars. CONTAINMENTS: cv2-interactive hand-off boxes, cv2-note/cv2-comment quotes, the acks block (verbatim oEmbed titles + the converter's own ❗ ack-todo markers), tag attributes, the {CODE}_interactives.txt hand-off, self-reflection emoji IMAGES (img assets) — all untouched.
rules.overrides_gold_notes: The gold library largely ALREADY follows the rule (CEDT104 and ARFUN02 golds carry almost none of their WTs' emoji) — but the gold KEEPS emoji at some sites the rule strips: TEDC402's five feelings-scale faces (😎🙂😐😬🤯 in built tabs panes), scattered singles (OSBY301 and similar), TRR109/110 + XGF9001 + BLL120/252 + XDLS908, and the gold keeps ➡/🡪 arrow FORMS where the converter uses the plain-arrow form (TEDC401). All are INTENTIONAL CL-0051 overrides. THE WATCH CLASS: MXDI201/ENGS102-style emoji-as-CONTENT (vocab/description cards where the emoji IS the referent — the gold keeps them on MXDI201) lives INSIDE cv2-interactive hand-off boxes on the converter side, so the strip does not touch it; any widget build that renders that content live must revisit the carve-out question with this entry as the reference.
rules.v2_home: Data Input_Doc_Rules.emoji_strip (exempt list VERBATIM from the ledger + exempt_extensions.maths_operators + arrow_map, all data-editable); engine ListsAndRuns.EmojiStrip (the LinkTextDisplay post-pass seam — runs AFTER all tag machinery, so the ✅-glued [TITLE BAR] fences (OSSC), the ✅[Tile] delimiters, the title splits and the 🔴 red-run sentinels are untouchable BY CONSTRUCTION); wired in PageAssembler before LinkTextDisplay, stopping at the acks block.

rules.name:
A writer's explicit go-to-journal button ships the templated

Go to your journal

inside the activity box
rules.rule:
A [button] whose EXPLICIT label folds to 'go to (your) journal' — or the alias-typed [go to journal]/[journal button] span — renders as the design team's templated

Go to your journal

INSIDE the open activity box (a bundle-owned activity absorbs a directly-following such button into the box before it closes), never as a green
. A button carrying a URL, and a bare [Button] whose label came only from the journal_label_default, keep the existing button behaviour.
rules.overrides_gold_notes: The gold library is ERA-MIXED: both <h4 class=goJournal> and <div class=button>Go to journal occur widely, MIXED within most subjects (no group discriminator). The developer's SCCH302 feedback names the h4 as the design team's CURRENT convention, so this is a forward-looking overrides-gold rule: divergence from a button-form gold at a go-to-journal site is an INTENTIONAL design-team override — never move it back toward the gold.

rules.name: Every content image ships alt text (verified iStock API title > URL-slug Title-Case) + loading="lazy"
rules.rule: A content image's alt attribute is populated from the asset's title — the VERIFIED iStock API title when the *_istock-acks.txt map covers the id, else the URL slug Title-Cased (the slug-is-title rule); nothing derivable → alt stays empty (never invent a description). Every content also carries loading="lazy". Applies to the Mode-P visible placeholder, the Mode-P commented-out real reference (the tag the developer copies out), and the Mode-D direct , on free-body AND table-cell images.
rules.overrides_gold_notes: The gold library is ERA-MIXED: most gold images have an alt (much of it hand-typed editorial text like 'Beautification image'), but only a minority carry loading="lazy" (older modules predate the convention). The developer's SCCH302 feedback names the iStock API title + loading="lazy" as the design team's CURRENT convention, so this is a forward-looking overrides-gold rule: alt/loading divergence from the gold at any content image is an INTENTIONAL design-team override — never move it back toward the gold (neither toward its hand-typed alts nor toward its lazy-less era).

rules.status: CAPTURED (already satisfied live — the rule stops the gold's violations being copied)
rules.name: No col-md-8 nested directly inside another col-md-8
rules.rule: An inner row inside a col-md-8 wrapper never uses col-md-8 — use col-md-12 col-12 (or a documented inner pattern). col-8-in-col-12 and col-12-in-col-8 are both fine. Applies to inner activity col-8 too.

rules.measured_note: The converter never emits a direct col-md-8>row>col-md-8 chain. Some gold pages carry the violating nest (they predate the rule) — a divergence matching this rule is an INTENTIONAL override, never moved toward the gold.

rules.rule: A carousel .viewer nested inside a col-md-8 wrapper uses col-md-12 col-12; a standalone one prefers col-md-8 col-12 (col-md-12 permitted for large content / book-page images). All carousel types alike.

The gold is col-md-12-dominant, consistent with the rule. No code change needed.

rules.rule: A built speech-bubble image column takes inner-side padding: left-positioned image -> paddingR, right-positioned -> paddingL; never mirror a sibling that pads both sides the same.
